Black Sea and Adjara

Four days in the west: Kutaisi, Kobuleti, Batumi, Gonio, Makhuntseti and Mtirala.

days
4 / 3 nights
Total distance
880 km
Total driving
14:30
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
May–October
Difficulty
Moderate

Click a marker for details. Coloured lines are ready-made road trips.

Tbilisi to Batumi is 370 kilometres and five and a half hours — a full driving day that is much better broken with a stop in Kutaisi. Four days gives you both halves of Adjara: the coast and the mountains behind it. Batumi is not only a beach; half an hour inland the subtropical forest and the waterfalls begin.

Day one is mostly driving, with Kutaisi as the break. Day two runs along the coast: the long pebble beach of Kobuleti, the Batumi Botanical Garden on Green Cape with its Japanese, Himalayan and Mediterranean sections spilling down to the sea, and finally Batumi itself — the boulevard, the old town and the lit-up towers at night. Day three heads south to Gonio-Apsaros Fortress, a Roman castellum where, by tradition, the Apostle Matthias is buried. Day four goes up into the hills: the Adjaristsqali valley, the arched stone bridge and waterfall at Makhuntseti, then Mtirala National Park, the wettest place in Georgia.

Take the climate seriously: Adjara receives up to 2,500 millimetres of rain a year and summer downpours are common. Some sections inside Mtirala and up the valley need real ground clearance. The swimming season runs June to September, while May and October are excellent for the mountains, the waterfalls and the empty coastal road.

Day-by-day plan

Day 1 · Tbilisi → Kutaisi → Batumi (370 km, 5 h 30 min) - 08:00 Leave Tbilisi on the E60. - 11:30 Kutaisi: Bagrati Cathedral and lunch (2 h). - 17:00 Arrive Batumi, check in, evening on the boulevard (2 h). - Overnight in Batumi.

Day 2 · Kobuleti and the Botanical Garden (90 km, 1 h 30 min) - 09:30 Drive north to Kobuleti for the beach and promenade (2 h 30 min). - 13:00 Lunch in Kobuleti (1 h). - 15:00 Batumi Botanical Garden on Green Cape (2 h 30 min). - 19:00 Batumi old town and Piazza (1 h 30 min). - Overnight in Batumi.

Day 3 · Gonio and Batumi (40 km, 1 h) - 10:00 Gonio-Apsaros Fortress and its museum (1 h 30 min). - 12:00 Beach time at Gonio or Kvariati (2 h). - 15:00 Late lunch at a seafront restaurant (1 h 30 min). - 18:00 Batumi cable car and the Alphabet Tower (2 h). - Overnight in Batumi.

Day 4 · Makhuntseti, Mtirala → Tbilisi (400 km, 6 h 30 min) - 08:00 Up the Adjaristsqali valley to the Makhuntseti bridge and waterfall (1 h 30 min). - 10:30 Mtirala National Park, short trail and suspension bridge (2 h). - 13:00 Lunch in Chakvi or Kobuleti (1 h). - 14:30 Drive back via Samtredia and Kutaisi. - 21:00 Back in Tbilisi.

Stops on this route

Town

Bagrati Cathedral and central Kutaisi

The cathedral on Ukimerioni hill and the old streets of Kutaisi spread out below it.

3 h
Beach

Kobuleti Beach and Protected Areas

A quieter resort town north of Batumi — a long pebble beach and a rare peat bog reserve.

4 h
Nature

Batumi Botanical Garden

Over a hundred hectares on a cape above the sea, with nine floristic zones of the world laid out side by side.

3 h
Town

Batumi Boulevard and Old Town

A seven-kilometre seafront promenade, a nineteenth-century old quarter and modern towers in one compact city.

6 h
Fortress

Gonio-Apsaros Fortress

A Roman military fort south of Batumi — 18 towers, active excavations and a grave traditionally linked to an apostle.

2 h
Waterfall

Makhuntseti Waterfall and Arched Bridge

A thirty-metre waterfall and a medieval stone arch bridge in the Adjaristsqali valley, an hour from Batumi.

2 h
Nature

Mtirala National Park

Colchic rainforest behind Batumi — one of the wettest places in Europe, with trails, a waterfall and a zipline.

4 h

Tips

  • It rains often in Adjara — pack a waterproof and a spare pair of shoes even in summer.
  • The park road inside Mtirala and parts of the valley need proper ground clearance.
  • Parking in Batumi is expensive and scarce in summer; choose a hotel with its own parking.
  • The beaches are pebble, not sand (except Ureki) — water shoes make a real difference.
  • Coastal prices double in July and August; May, June and September are calmer and cheaper.
  • Tbilisi-Batumi is 5 h 30 min in one go — plan an early start on day one.
